title: Repository instructions for agents
summary: Keep one short AGENTS.md at the repository root for what the README does not say, and point host files at it.

sections.label: What the file is
sections.text: AGENTS.md is plain Markdown at the repository root with no required fields. The agents.md site calls it a README for agents and lists Codex, Copilot, Cursor and Gemini CLI as readers. Claude Code targets under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. This practice adopts that limit.

sections.label: What to put in it
items: Commands to build, test and lint.
Repository structure an agent cannot infer quickly.
Conventions that differ from tool defaults.
Boundaries as always, ask first and never.
Only what the README does not say.

sections.label: What to leave out
sections.text: The Claude Code doctor checkup trims directory layouts, dependency lists and architecture overviews and keeps pitfalls, rationale and conventions that differ from tool defaults. The evaluation below found that repository overviews did not help. Claude Code sends a multi step procedure to a skill and a partial rule to a path scoped rule.

sections.label: How hosts read it
sections.text: Codex takes one file per directory, AGENTS.override.md before AGENTS.md, concatenates them from the root down to the working directory and stops at a default 32 KiB. Copilot reads AGENTS.md anywhere in the repository and the nearest file takes precedence. Claude Code reads AGENTS.md only when no CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md sits in the working directory or above it, and a CLAUDE.md can import it with an @AGENTS.md line. Keep host specific files as pointers, not copies.

sections.label: What the evidence says
sections.text: Developer written files raised success on a new CTXbench set by about 2.4 percent, a gain the authors call marginal and not statistically significant. Model generated files lowered resolution by 0.5 percent on SWE-bench and 2 percent on CTXbench and raised cost by 20 and 23 percent. Removing the testing section cut cost by about a fifth on CTXbench with no significant change in accuracy. File length showed no clear dependency with success or cost. The authors recommend including only what agents need that the README lacks. One study with particular agents and models does not predict your project.

sections.label: What Atlas provides
sections.text: The full pack contains an AGENTS.md written from project.json with purpose, commands, workflow, roles, skills, acceptance, boundaries and practices sections. It says it does not run anything, configure an integration or grant a permission. Selecting this practice adds its label and application to the Practices section and records its sources in SOURCES.md.

sections.label: Check in your environment
sections.text: Confirm which host reads the file and whether a CLAUDE.md or copilot-instructions.md shadows it. Run every listed command and remove any that fails. In Claude Code, /doctor prompt-audit covers AGENTS.md and reports stale references and contradictions without changing files. Claude Code treats these files as context, not enforced configuration, so a rule that must always hold needs a hook or a setting.

basis: Documented host behavior, research findings and proposed practice
confidence: Host behavior and study figures have scoped sources read on 2026-10-11. The content list and the line limit are a proposed practice, not a measured result.

catalog.applicability: Use when a repository is worked on by coding agents and needs one shared place for commands, conventions and boundaries.
catalog.limits: The file is written context for an agent. It does not configure a host, grant a permission or prove that its instructions were followed.
